facts.raw_span: A 44-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
he had a history of hypertension
he had a history of cervical disc herniation
he underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
his father had progressive cognitive decline and imbalance since the age of 50 years
his father died of cerebral hemorrhage at the age of 65 years
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes
Neurological examination revealed bilateral Babinski sign
T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showing lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
Showing a lobe-dominant distribution of multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions, mainly involving bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
Revealed a heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
a 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance

concepts.why: The patient's MRI shows lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities, and the presence of cerebral microbleeds, which are consistent with cerebral amyloid angiopathy, a condition associated with the HTRA1 gene mutation.
The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of brisk bilateral tendon reflexes and bilateral Babinski sign are consistent with hypertensive encephalopathy.

aliases: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
concepts.why: The patient's family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance, and the presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities, are consistent with CADASIL syndrome.
The patient's history of cervical disc herniation and the presence of brisk bilateral tendon reflexes and bilateral Babinski sign are consistent with cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
The patient underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale, which is a known risk factor for stroke.
The patient's HTRA1 gene mutation and the presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities are consistent with HTRA1-related cerebral small vessel disease.
The patient's MRI shows lacunar infarctions, which are consistent with lacunar stroke.
The patient's MRI shows cerebral microbleeds, which are consistent with cerebral amyloid angiopathy or other small vessel diseases.

rationales.F06: Family history of cerebral hemorrhage increases the likelihood of Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy and HTRA1-Related Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
rationales.F09: Lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities are common in Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy, CADASIL Syndrome, and Lacunar Stroke.
rationales.F10: Lobe-dominant distribution of cerebral microbleeds is characteristic of Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy and HTRA1-Related Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
rationales.F11: Heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene is diagnostic of HTRA1-Related Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
